what_it_does: Graph databases let you search for shortest paths or other connections between pairs of nodes — for example, 'find me the path from city A to city B.' When you run many such pair queries at the same time, the hardware struggles because the memory accesses are messy and unpredictable: two queries might need the same chunk of graph data, but the processor fetches it twice from the slow main memory chip instead of sharing it. PairGraph is a custom hardware accelerator (a chip built for this specific job) that looks at the structure of the graph before processing queries, identifies which parts of the graph multiple queries will both visit, and routes those queries so they can share the fetched data. By reusing intermediate results rather than redundantly loading the same graph topology over and over from main memory, PairGraph cuts down on expensive off-chip memory traffic and speeds up concurrent pairwise graph queries.
